title: Friuli-Venezia Giulia's GPL Prices Barely Move While Italy's Climb — A Quiet Regional Discount Emerges
dek: As national LPG prices rise for a fourth straight week, drivers in Friuli-Venezia Giulia are increasingly paying less than the rest of Italy at the pump.
executive_summary: Today's self-service prices in Friuli-Venezia Giulia stand at €2.024/L for Benzina, €2.276/L for Gasolio, €0.765/L for GPL and €2.199/kg for Metano — essentially flat to slightly lower than two days ago (Benzina and Gasolio each eased about 0.3%, while GPL and Metano held exactly steady). Against the national same-day averages of €2.020/L, €2.258/L, €0.792/L and €2.075/kg respectively, the region is running a small premium on Benzina, Gasolio and Metano, but now sits 3.4% cheaper than the rest of Italy on GPL. The region's 471 reporting stations out of 522 registered (90.2%) are in line with the national reporting rate of 90.4%.

The more interesting story sits in the weekly data. Benzina and Gasolio both peaked regionally in the week of September 21 and have eased for six straight tracked weeks since, with Friuli-Venezia Giulia's pullback slightly outpacing the national retreat. Metano has climbed sharply nationwide since midsummer, and while the region still carries a persistent premium on it, that premium has been narrowing as national prices catch up. But GPL is the real divergence: national LPG prices have risen for four consecutive tracked weeks while Friuli-Venezia Giulia's have moved less than a third of a cent — flipping a market that was essentially at parity in early October into a region now noticeably cheaper than the rest of the country.

fuel_sections.heading: Petrol Eases for a Sixth Straight Week Off Its September Peak
paragraphs: Self-service Benzina in Friuli-Venezia Giulia closed at €2.024/L today, down about 0.3% from €2.030/L two days ago, and running a thin €0.004/L (+0.2%) premium over the national average of €2.020/L.

Zoomed out, Benzina peaked regionally in the week of September 21 at €2.194/L (nationally €2.167/L) and has declined every tracked week since, down 7.6% to today's €2.027/L weekly average — a sharper pullback than the national 6.7% decline from the same peak. Over the full tracked period since late July, the region's Benzina price is up just 1.5%, compared with 2.3% nationally, meaning Friuli-Venezia Giulia rode the September run-up by less and has since corrected it more aggressively than the rest of Italy.

fuel_sections.heading: Diesel Mirrors Petrol's Retreat From the September Highs
paragraphs: Self-service Gasolio in the region priced at €2.276/L today, down roughly 0.3% from €2.284/L two days prior, and €0.018/L (+0.8%) above the national average of €2.258/L.

Like Benzina, Gasolio peaked in the week of September 21 at a regional weekly average of €2.405/L (national €2.374/L) and has fallen in most tracked weeks since, down 5.2% to date versus a 4.8% national decline from that peak. Across the full tracked span, the region's diesel price is up 3.0% since late July, slightly trailing the 4.0% national rise — a milder round-trip for Friuli-Venezia Giulia than for the country as a whole.

fuel_sections.heading: While Italy's LPG Prices Climb, Friuli-Venezia Giulia Holds the Line
paragraphs: GPL priced at €0.765/L in the region today, unchanged from two days ago, and now €0.027/L (3.4%) below the national average of €0.792/L — the region's largest discount of any tracked fuel.

The divergence has built over the last month: national GPL prices have risen in every tracked week since the week of October 5, up 2.2% in that stretch (from €0.770/L to €0.787/L), while Friuli-Venezia Giulia's barely moved, up just 0.3% over the same weeks (€0.763/L to €0.765/L). Over the full tracked period since late July, the region's GPL is up 1.7% versus 3.7% nationally — a market that was close to even in early autumn has split into a clear regional discount.

fuel_sections.heading: Natural Gas Keeps Its Regional Premium, But Italy Is Closing the Gap
paragraphs: Metano held at €2.199/kg in Friuli-Venezia Giulia today, unchanged from two days ago, and €0.124/kg (6.0%) above the national average of €2.075/kg — the largest premium of any fuel tracked in the region.

Both have climbed sharply since midsummer: the region's Metano is up 29.4% since late July (from €1.699/kg), while the national average has risen even faster, up 35.3% (from €1.500/kg) over the same span. That faster national climb has narrowed the region's premium from roughly €0.20/kg in late July to about €0.17/kg today, even as the region continues to pay more for Metano than most of the country.

network_section.heading: A Stable, Well-Reporting Network
paragraphs: Friuli-Venezia Giulia has 522 registered stations today, one fewer than two days ago, of which 471 are actively reporting prices — a 90.2% reporting rate.

That is essentially in line with Italy's national reporting rate of 90.4% (21,648 of 23,934 registered stations), suggesting the region's price data is about as complete and timely as the country's as a whole; the small week-to-week shifts in registered-station counts reflect normal churn rather than any reporting disruption.

methodology_section.heading: How This Report Gets Made, Automatically, Every Day
paragraphs: This entire report — the price data, the weekly trend analysis, the choice of which region to spotlight, and the writing itself — is generated automatically every day by an unattended pipeline built with Claude Code. Each morning the pipeline pulls Italy's official MIMIT fuel-price feed, rotates through the country's 20 regions on a deterministic, self-correcting schedule, computes the weekly regional-versus-national comparisons, and drafts the analysis from the resulting numbers.

That stands in contrast to how this kind of regional reporting is usually done: a person manually downloading spreadsheets, re-typing figures into Excel, and writing commentary by hand, day after day. Here, no spreadsheet is maintained and no number is retyped — the dashboard, the trend analysis and this report all update themselves from the same automated pipeline.

caption:
Today's regional spotlight: Friuli-Venezia Giulia. While most of Italy has watched GPL (LPG) prices climb for four straight tracked weeks, this region's auto-gas prices have barely moved — turning what was close to an even market into a 3.4% regional discount at the pump versus the national average.

Fuel Dashboard is a free, self-updating site that tracks petrol, diesel, LPG and natural gas prices across all of Italy's regions, provinces, municipalities and 300+ brands, refreshed every morning from Italy's official MIMIT price feed. No one is manually re-typing numbers into a spreadsheet — the data pull, the regional spotlight rotation, the weekly trend analysis, and even the writing of this report are generated automatically, every day, by an unattended pipeline built with Claude Code.

That's the real pitch: a small AI-assisted build can replace what used to need a standing team and a manually maintained Excel file — the same underlying data, continuously refreshed, behind a live interactive dashboard instead of a static sheet.
